candidates.title: Why the Great Salt Lake is two colors
candidates.central_question: Why does one half of the lake look pink-red and the other blue-green?
candidates.primary_intent: why is Great Salt Lake two colors / half red half blue
candidates.competition: Local news + NASA EO + USGS pages answer pieces; few unified visual mechanism pages with causeway+microbiology+satellite time series.
candidates.waypoint_advantage: USGS 50-year satellite change + NASA EO algae imagery + annotated causeway salinity map + Dashboard/Scenes outdoor Utah light context

candidates.title: Why the Okavango Delta floods in the dry season
candidates.central_question: How can a desert wetland flood months after local rains stop?
candidates.primary_intent: why does Okavango Delta flood in dry season
candidates.competition: Safari blogs dominate; science explainers exist but visual lag/travel-time storytelling is weak.
candidates.waypoint_advantage: Flood-pulse travel-time map from Angola highlands + seasonal satellite wet/dry compare

candidates.title: What carved the Eye of the Sahara?

candidates.title: Satellites caught these dunes moving

candidates.title: When does the desert become a sea?

candidates.title: Why does this landscape look like a flood carved it?

candidates.title: How can a rainforest grow on pure sand?
candidates.central_question: How does tall rainforest survive on nutrient-poor sand dunes?

candidates.competition: Tourism + parks pages; mechanism (mycelium/nutrient cycling/dune succession) often underserved visually.
candidates.waypoint_advantage: Dune-age vegetation succession diagram + nutrient-loop graphic + related Lençóis sand/water contrast

candidates.title: Why do valleys fill with fog at dawn?
candidates.location: Temperate mountain/river valleys (global pattern; Appalachian/US examples)
candidates.central_question: Why does fog pool in valleys overnight and vanish after sunrise?
candidates.primary_intent: why does fog form in valleys / morning valley fog
candidates.competition: NWS explainers exist; few pages combine satellite dendritic fog image + cold-air drainage diagram + field noticing guide.
candidates.waypoint_advantage: NOAA satellite dendritic example + drainage diagram + Dashboard morning-conditions / photo timing link

candidates.title: Why do these clouds look like UFOs — and stay still?

candidates.central_question: How can a cloud look solid and stationary while air is racing through it?
candidates.primary_intent: what causes lenticular clouds / UFO clouds mountains
candidates.competition: Met Office/Wikipedia/popular photo galleries; mechanism+standing-wave diagram under-served for photographers.
candidates.waypoint_advantage: Standing-wave cross-section + photo-timing notes for Scenes/Photo Coach + Cascade link to rain-shadow story

candidates.title: What 40 years of satellites reveal about one glacier
